- The title and alt_text are published with the item: adds_information is also true if either states anything (a date, name, place, event, award or description) that the holder's page does not show or say.
- Approved rights rule: The project's approved rights rule for Library of Congress and National Archives items (user decision 2026-10-09). It applies only to a source whose registry standing is the Library of Congress (loc.gov) or the U.S. National Archives (archives.gov), and only to the holder's own rights field in that source's snapshot. Library of Congress: a rights advisory that reads "No known restrictions on publication" (that sentence, alone or followed by further sentences) means license_class public-domain. National Archives: a use restriction status of "Unrestricted" (useRestriction.status, a record created by the federal government; never the access restriction) means license_class public-domain. Library of Congress "Publication may be restricted" or "Rights status not evaluated", and National Archives use restriction "Restricted", "Restricted - Possibly", "Restricted - Partly", "Restricted - Fully", "Undetermined", mean the item is never usable: license_class must be unknown or rights-restricted. Public domain under this rule needs the rights_statement to be the holder's exact wording from that field. The rule never applies to a Wikimedia Commons file page or tag, or to any other host; there, license_class follows strictly from the holder's own statement.

verdict: "supported" only if quote_in_snapshot, entailed, atomic and source_type_ok are all true, adds_information is false, and quote_in_live is "yes" ("unreachable" is acceptable only for sources fetched by http or api). "refuted" if a quote or statement is missing, or the evidence contradicts or does not support the record. Otherwise "unclear".
rationale: at most two sentences naming the specific problem, or "no problem found".
registry_suggestion: null, unless a source not listed in the authority registry is published by an archive, museum, government body, university, foundation or prize body that could be listed; then one line naming the publisher, its domain and the type it could have (for example "fi.edu: The Franklin Institute, institutional"). It is advice for a person who maintains the registry: it never changes another field or the verdict.

Return only JSON of this shape, with exactly one entry for each item above and each item's id exactly as written:
{"verdicts": [{"id": "<item id>", "verdict": "supported|refuted|unclear", "quote_in_snapshot": true|false, "quote_in_live": "yes|no|unreachable", "entailed": true|false, "adds_information": true|false, "atomic": true|false, "source_type_ok": true|false, "rationale": "<text>", "registry_suggestion": "<text>"|null}]}
